answer_1.quote: We study the nature of unconditional modes (highest‑scoring outputs) of various kinds of autoregressive models, aiming to characterize the degenerate behaviors observed ... (a) the MarianMT Chinese‑English encoder‑decoder machine translation model (b) a 345M‑parameter GPT‑2 model finetuned on the ROC stories dataset (story generation) (c) a 7B‑parameter general‑purpose base LLaMA model, as well as finetuned Alpaca and Guanaco variants.
answer_1.outputs: text sequences such as translations, story completions, and instruction responses

answer_2.quote: Table 2 also shows BLEU and BLEURT scores of these translations, and we report perplexity under the Llama2‑7B model as a fluency measure.

answer_3.quote: We use a reward model from Open Assistant to score outputs and also perform pairwise comparisons with GPT‑4, asking it to choose the better response.

answer_4.quote: Human raters, GPT‑4, and the original reward model all prefer the conditioned outputs on average. Annotators were instructed to decide which response is better and could label A or B.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were told to compare two responses and select the one with higher overall quality; if equal, label '-'.
